description: Palestinian manakish and saj wraps baked to order at a counter, cheap and very fast. Open from breakfast to the small hours. A dependable low-cost meal when the day's budget has gone elsewhere.

name: Al Safadi
description: A large, permanently busy Lebanese restaurant on Sheikh Zayed Road, doing mezze and grills well into the night at fair prices. Copes easily with big groups and late arrivals, which is often exactly what is needed.

name: Emirates Palace Mandara Spa Cafe
description: A quiet café inside Emirates Palace known chiefly for its gold-flaked cappuccino, which is exactly as absurd and as photographed as it sounds. Calm, cool and a cheap way to see inside the building without dining there.

name: Al Fanar Abu Dhabi
description: The capital's branch of the Emirati heritage restaurant, styled as a 1960s home and sitting a short walk from the Corniche beach. Familiar menu, comfortable room and an easy family dinner after a day on the sand.

name: Shakespeare and Co Abu Dhabi
description: An all-day café with a long international menu and floral, slightly overstuffed decor. Not exciting, but open early, reliable with children and reasonably priced — the practical breakfast when the day starts before the museums do.

name: Saadiyat Beach Golf Club Terrace
description: A clubhouse terrace overlooking the fairways and the sea, where gazelles wander the course at dawn and dusk. Open to non-players, quiet and mid-priced. A calm lunch between the Saadiyat museums and the beach.

name: Mezlai
description: The country's first fine-dining Emirati restaurant, inside Emirates Palace, taking machboos and camel from the majlis to the tasting menu. Expensive and genuinely distinctive — the one high-end room here serving local food seriously.

name: Yas Island Observation Deck
description: An elevated deck overlooking the Yas Marina circuit and the island's parks, best at dusk when the track lighting comes on. Cheap, short and a good way to see the layout without paying for a circuit experience.

name: Abu Dhabi Falconry Show
description: A late-afternoon falconry demonstration in the desert margin, with birds flown to the lure and handlers explaining the tradition's place in Emirati life. Children can hold a falcon at the end. Booking needed.

name: Al Hosn Cultural Evening
description: Traditional music, craft demonstrations and storytelling in the Qasr Al Hosn grounds on cool-season evenings. Cheap, unhurried and considerably more atmospheric than a museum visit by daylight.

name: Saadiyat Turtle Watch Cruise
description: A morning boat trip along the Saadiyat coast looking for hawksbill turtles and dolphins, with a marine biologist aboard. Genuinely educational rather than a sightseeing loop. Early start and booking required.

name: Mangrove Night Kayak
description: A guided paddle into the mangroves after dark, when bioluminescent plankton light the water with every stroke. Minimum age fourteen and booking essential. Quiet, strange and among the most romantic things to do in the capital.

name: Al Bahar Corniche Walk
description: A free seafront promenade at the Corniche's eastern end, lined with low-key cafés and shaded seating facing the water. Costs nothing, works at any hour, and is the easiest way to close an evening in the city.

name: Umm Al Emarat Wellness Garden
description: A sensory and botanic garden within the main park, planted for scent and texture and threaded with shaded seating. Nominal entry, deliberately calm, and a good counterweight to a day of theme parks.

name: Yas Kartzone
description: A junior-friendly karting track separate from the main circuit, with cadet karts from about age six and two-seaters for a parent and child. Cheaper and gentler than the circuit sessions, and open into the evening.

name: Qasr Al Sarab Dune Walk
description: A guided walk into the Empty Quarter dunes from the Liwa resort, among the highest sand in the world. Sunrise and sunset departures only. A very long drive from the capital, and utterly unlike anywhere else in the country.

name: Sharjah Safari Park
description: The largest safari park outside Africa, holding more than fifty thousand animals across twelve African environments, toured by bus and on foot. Extraordinary value for the scale. Closed in high summer and a genuine full day.

name: Sharjah Aquarium Touch Pool
description: A supervised touch pool of starfish, sea cucumbers and small rays attached to the main aquarium, with staff explaining each species. Costs almost nothing and holds small children far longer than the tanks do.

name: Sharjah Desert Park
description: Three linked attractions — a natural history museum, an Arabian wildlife centre and a children's farm — covering the region's own species properly. Extremely cheap, largely indoors and a serious half-day for animal-minded children.

name: Al Qasba Canal Boat
description: A short covered boat ride along the Al Qasba canal and out into the lagoon, past the observation wheel and the fountain. Cheap, brief and pleasant after dark when the whole waterfront is lit.

name: Sharjah Heart of Sharjah Walk
description: The restored old town of coral-stone houses, courtyards and narrow sikkas, free to wander and largely traffic-free. Several museums open off it, but the walk itself costs nothing and is the better part of the experience.

name: Sharjah Calligraphy Museum
description: A small, beautifully quiet museum devoted to Arabic calligraphy, housed in a restored courtyard building in the old town. Nearly free, rarely busy and a restful forty minutes between larger stops.

name: Al Hisn Sharjah
description: The rebuilt ruler's fort at the centre of the old town, holding the emirate's own history from pearling through to the oil years. Cheap, cool and compact — an hour is enough to see it properly.

name: Kalba Mangrove Centre
description: A protected mangrove reserve on the east coast holding the oldest trees in Arabia and a rare kingfisher found almost nowhere else. Boardwalks, kayaks and hides. Cheap, calm and a world away from the west-coast beaches.

name: Khorfakkan Corniche Cafe Row
description: A line of simple cafés along the Khorfakkan seafront serving karak, grills and fresh juice with tables facing the bay. Cheap and unhurried, and effectively the only mid-day option on this stretch of coast.

name: Sharjah Golf and Shooting Club
description: Indoor ranges for archery, clay and target shooting with instruction included, plus a driving range outside. Minimum age sixteen for the ranges. Air-conditioned and an unusual option for a group of adults on a hot afternoon.

name: Ajman Dhow Yard
description: One of the last working dhow-building yards in the Gulf, where wooden hulls are still shaped by eye without plans. Free to watch from the roadside, entirely unstaged, and genuinely absorbing for anyone who likes making things.

name: Al Zorah Golf Terrace
description: A clubhouse terrace looking over the mangroves and the golf course, where flamingos are often visible from the table. Open to non-players, quiet and reasonably priced. A calm lunch after a morning on the water.

name: Ajman Corniche Night Market
description: An evening market along the corniche with craft stalls, food carts and small fairground rides through the cooler months. Free to walk and cheap to eat at — an easy, unplanned way to fill a night.

name: Ajman Beach Cafe
description: A simple seafront café serving breakfast, grills and karak with tables a few metres from the sand. Cheap, quick and useful either side of a beach afternoon on a coast with limited options.

name: Ajman Marina Cruise
description: A quiet ninety-minute cruise out of Ajman creek past the dhow yards and along the corniche at sunset. Considerably cheaper than the Dubai equivalents and rarely more than half full.

name: UAQ Old Town Walk
description: The half-abandoned old town on the UAQ peninsula, with coral-stone houses, a watchtower and the fort at its centre, free to wander and almost entirely empty. Quietly atmospheric and utterly untouristed.

name: UAQ Mangrove Beach
description: A quiet free beach where the mangroves meet the sand, with flamingos often wading at the far end. No facilities and almost no people. Bring shade and water; take everything away again.

name: UAQ Fish Market
description: A small working fish market where the morning catch is sold on ice and grilled to order at the stalls behind. Cheap, entirely local and about as fresh as it gets on this coast.

name: Dreamland Camping Ground
description: Shaded lawns and camping pitches attached to the aqua park, open separately for day use with barbecue areas and a lake. Cheap and green in a stretch of coast that is largely neither.

name: Al Sinniyah Island Boat Trip
description: A boat out to a protected island holding one of the region's largest Socotra cormorant colonies, with dolphins often on the way. Booking required and genuinely off the tourist track. Bring binoculars.

name: RAK Al Hamra Marina Walk
description: A free marina promenade lined with cafés and moored boats, pleasant to walk at either end of the day. Quiet, well kept and an easy no-cost way to fill the hour before dinner.

name: Jebel Jais Camping Site
description: Terraced camping pitches high on Jebel Jais with fire pits, clean facilities and some of the darkest skies in the country. Cool-season only and booking required. Worth staying past sunset for the stars alone.

name: RAK Camel Racing Track
description: Early morning camel training and races, free to watch from the rail while owners follow along the parallel track in 4x4s. Entirely unstaged and quite unlike anything else. Winter mornings only, and you need to be there by seven.

name: Iceland Water Park
description: A large penguin-themed water park with a wave pool, a rain dance floor and slides across a wide range of nerve. Considerably cheaper than the Dubai parks and much less crowded midweek.

name: Bear Grylls Rope Course
description: A high ropes and obstacle course on Jebel Jais, harnessed throughout, accessible from about seven. Less extreme than the via ferrata and a good way for a mixed-age group to do the mountain together.

name: Al Rams Fishing Village
description: A working fishing harbour north of RAK where the boats come in through the morning and nets are mended on the quay. Free, unstaged and photogenic. Go early if the point is to see it actually working.

name: RAK Corniche Seafood Grill
description: A creekside grill serving the day's catch simply, with tables out on the corniche. Cheap for the quality, popular with local families and a good deal more characterful than the resort restaurants down the coast.

name: Al Marjan Beachfront Dining
description: A row of beachfront restaurants on Al Marjan facing due west, so dinner and sunset arrive together. Mid-priced, unhurried and considerably quieter than the equivalent strip in Dubai.

name: Fujairah Corniche Park
description: A free seafront park along the Fujairah corniche with play areas, shaded lawns and a walking track facing the Gulf of Oman. Costs nothing and works as an easy last stop before the drive home.

name: Wadi Shawka Pools
description: A free mountain wadi with clear pools, a marked hiking loop and a dam at the top, popular with local families at weekends. Rough underfoot and no facilities. Genuinely beautiful and costs nothing at all.

name: Fujairah Heritage Village
description: A reconstructed village of palm-frond and mudbrick houses beside the Ain Al Madhab springs, showing how the east coast lived before oil. Nearly free and quick, and it pairs naturally with the gardens next door.

name: Snoopy Island Dive Centre
description: Try-dives and guided reef dives off Al Aqah, with equipment and instructor included. Minimum age twelve for the introductory dive and medical questions apply. The clearest water in the country and the only real diving on this list.

name: Fujairah Friday Market
description: A sprawling roadside market on the mountain highway selling carpets, pottery, fruit and honey, open every day despite the name. Free to browse, cheerfully chaotic and a natural break on the drive across from the west coast.

name: Al Aqah Sunset Paddleboard
description: Stand-up paddleboarding on the calm evening water off Al Aqah, with the mountains going pink behind. Boards and buoyancy aids included, minimum age eight. Cheap and considerably gentler than the snorkel trips.

name: Dibba Al Fujairah Corniche
description: A free beach and promenade at the northern end of the east coast, calm and almost empty midweek, with the Musandam mountains visible up the coast. No facilities beyond a few cafés on the road behind.
